ap stores Entry<V> = { value: V, expiresAt?: number }
  - pruneExpired() removes all expired entries
  - size and keys() call pruneExpired() to reflect only live entries
  - get() checks expiration, moves entry to MRU if valid

Usage examples
- Global TTL, default never-expire
  - const cache = new LRUCache<string, number>(100)
- Global TTL of 1 second
  - const cache = new LRUCache<string, number>(100, { ttl: 1000 })
- Per-entry TTL override
  - cache.set('a', 1, 500) // expires in 500ms
  - cache.set('b', 2) // uses global TTL if defined, otherwise never expires
- Testability
  - const cache = new LRUCache<string, string>(50, { now: () => clock.now })
  - clock is controlled in tests

Files touched
- src/lru.ts
  - Replaced simple Map<K, V> with Map<K, Entry<V>>
  - Added LRUCacheOptions, Entry<V>, and TTL logic
  - Implemented nowFn, pruneExpired, and updated size/keys/get/set/has accordingly

Notes
- This introduces a breaking-ish API change at construction time (accepting an options object). If you have existing call sites that rely on the old signature, you can migrate by passing an options object as the second argument or adjust TypeScript typings to support an overload. The runtime remains backwards tolerant if you pass an unknown second arg (it will be treated as no options and a default TTL of undefined).

If you want, I can add a small overload to preserve the old constructor signature (accepting either a number or an options object) to minimize migration friction.
